card.title: Short Story 7 — A Very Old Man with Enormous Wings (Gabriel García Márquez)

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: ## The story at a glance "A Very Old Man with Enormous Wings" by Gabriel García Márquez is magical realism's most famous lesson: an angel falls into a poor family's courtyard during a storm, and the neighbourhood's response is to charge admission.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Magical realism: the angel treated as a sideshow — miracle meets mundane cruelty.
Compare with the spider-woman: people prefer a moral story to a mystery.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Trick 3: The spider-woman outdraws the angel because her story has a MORAL — the satire on audiences preferring clear lessons to mystery; explain this comparison.  ·  ## The characters worth an essay **The old man with wings** is the story's sacred centre and its most passive figure: patient, silent, endureing — his divinity consists precisely in refusing to perform. He is an angel who fails every test the village sets (he does not understand Latin, does not heal on demand, does not fit the iconography) and whose only miracle is survival.…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: ## The themes worth an essay **The human response to the miraculous** — the central theme: given an angel, the village builds a ticket booth; the story argues that wonder is the first casualty of habit. **Cruelty and indifference** — the crowd's pokes and burns, the couple's cage and final relief: the theme that the sacred is treated as the villagers treat each other.…  ·  ## NEB short answers, solved **Q. How do Pelayo and Elisenda treat the old man with wings? (2 marks)** A. As a problem and then as an asset: they cage him in the chicken coop, charge admission to see him, grow rich on the crowds, and neglect him when the audience moves on. Their treatment is practical rather than reverent — the sacred handled like livestock. **Q.…

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Q. How do the villagers treat the angel? (2 marks) — as a carnival curiosity: caged in the chicken coop, charged admission, poked with iron.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ## NEB long answers, solved **Q. "The story is a satire of human response to the miraculous." Discuss with evidence. (8 marks)** A model answer gathers the satire's targets in order: the couple's ticket booth (the sacred monetised), the crowd's cruelty (pokes, burns, the iron), the church's credentialism (Father Gonzaga's Latin and correspondence), and the spider-woman's triumph (morality as better theatre than…  ·  **‘A Very Old Man with Enormous Wings’ — magical realism map (classified)** | Element | Matter-of-fact tone | Impossible content | |---|---|---| | Angel’s arrival | Reported like weather | Wings, old man | | Pelayo/Elisenda | Practical concerns | Chicken coop for angel | | Spider-woman | Fair attraction | Girl turned spider | | Miracles | Commodified | Ticket sales |

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## The plot, retold with an eye on its turns The discovery is deliberately undramatic: after three days of rain, crabs in the house, a sick child, and a smell the sea has left, Pelayo finds an old man with enormous wings lying face-down in the courtyard, dressed like a ragpicker, with only a few faded hairs left on his skull.…  ·  ## The devices, with evidence - **Magical realism** — the story's master technique: the angel is narrated in the same flat, domestic tone as the crabs and the rain, so that the fantastic enters the ordinary without ceremony — and the reader's unease is the point: we, like the villagers, cannot decide what to do with a miracle.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Magical realism: the angel is treated with mundane boredom (chickens, spider sideshow) — the extraordinary rendered ordinary is the genre's signature; define it with one example.  ·  Trick 2: Satire of human cruelty and credulity: villagers charge to see him, pluck feathers, then forget him — collect two acts of cruelty.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. Why does the spider-woman attract more visitors than the angel? (2 marks) — her clear moral tale is easier to consume than the angel's silent mystery.
